items.prompt: Which letter is silent in Spanish?
items.explanation: On its own, h is never pronounced: hola sounds like “ola”. (Ch is a separate sound, as in chocolate.)
optionNotes: J is a breathy sound from the throat, as in José.
Ñ sounds like ny in canyon.
R is a tap or a roll, never silent.

items.explanation: A word ending in a vowel, n or s is stressed on the second-to-last syllable: HA-blan.
optionNotes: The last syllable is stressed only when the word ends in another consonant (hotel) or has a written accent.
Every Spanish word has one strong syllable.
The stress rules are the same for everyone.

items.explanation: Perro has a rolled rr. Pero, with one tapped r, means “but”.
optionNotes: Pero means “but”: one r is a quick tap.

items.explanation: A Spanish question opens with ¿, and the question word cómo has a written accent.
optionNotes: It needs ¿ at the start and the accent on cómo.
A question needs ¿ at the start.
